<description>
fixes #33128

this picks up #33164

on a normal start (without `-reindex`), `CompleteChainstateInitialization()`
calls `LoadGenesisBlock()`, which writes the genesis block to `blk00000.dat`
unless the block index already contains it. if `blocks/index` was deleted,
then the index is empty, so genesis is _unconditionally_ written again
even though the file is still intact on disk and holds all the later blocks

that write eventually reaches `AllocateFileRange()`, which allocates
space from the start of the file. with `posix_fallocate()`, this only
reserves space. on platforms without it (e.g. OpenBSD, NetBSD), the
fallback writes zeroes over the requested range, replacing the blocks
that were already there

only after that, does the node notice that the chainstate no longer
matches the block index and fail with `"Error initializing block database"`,
asking for `-reindex`. by then, the blocks are already gone, so the reindex
finds the genesis only, reports success, and `getblockcount` returns `0`

---

this PR makes `LoadGenesisBlock()` read the genesis block back _from
disk first_ and only write it when it is not already there. if genesis
is already on disk, update the blockfile info with its position and
size so that the next block is written after it instead of overwriting it
</description>

```diff
-            LogError("Writing genesis block to disk failed");

+        FlatFilePos blockPos{0, 0};
+        // The block index may be missing or corrupted (e.g. after an
+        // incomplete shutdown or manual recovery) while block file 0
+        // still contains a valid genesis block from a previous run.
+        // Check for that first. Otherwise, WriteBlock() eventually
+        // reaches AllocateFileRange(), whose fallback on platforms without
+        // a real preallocation syscall cannot tell that the file already
+        // contains data beyond this point and may zero it out.
+        CBlock existing_block;
+        if (!m_blockman.ReadBlock(existing_block, blockPos, genesis_block.GetHash())) {
+            blockPos = m_blockman.WriteBlock(genesis_block, 0);
+            if (blockPos.IsNull()) {
+                LogError("Writing genesis block to disk failed");
+                return false;
+            }
         }
         CBlockIndex* pindex{m_blockman.AddToBlockIndex(genesis_block, m_best_header)};
         ReceivedBlockTransactions(genesis_block, pindex, blockPos);
```

[2026-11-07] c:6706531093 comment by winterrdog (contributor) (edited 2026-11-07):
changes:
- updated the PR description & title
- rebased and fixed conflicts from merged changes
- my earlier approach of the `ReadBlock()` check ([suggested](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35524#issuecomment-5742883004) by @sedited) read at `{0, 0}`, but block positions point past the 8-byte block header, so it never matched and genesis was always rewritten. now, it reads at `{0, STORAGE_HEADER_BYTES}`
- dropped the `AllocateFileRange()` changes i had [proposed earlier](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35524#issuecomment-5757418198) because they are not _exactly_ what is needed to resolve this issue albeit were an alternate fix, but at a much lower level
[2026-11-07] c:6708634908 comment by winterrdog (contributor):
changes:
- updated the commit message and PR description to reflect the changes.
- when genesis is already on disk, its blockfile info is now updated via `UpdateBlockInfo()`, so the next block is written after it instead of overwriting it. skipping this caused the `connect_block` fuzz target to [fail](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/actions/runs/42369614221/job/128394828567) because the next block overwrote genesis, causing `ReadBlock()` to fail the hash check.
